gates.why: An engine error is a broken capture.
A missing record means the capture is incomplete.
Only identical fonts and corpora are comparable.
Missing metric numbers and array elements must never disappear from statistics.

Advances within 0.02 px or 0.05% of the reference in 99.5% of covered cases. Against WebKit with its synthetic-bold rule the engine reaches 99.93%; Chromium against WebKit is 60.6%, all of it synthetic bold.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.
The line box sets the vertical position of every line. Chromium and WebKit report identical ascent and descent, so the engine must too. (Node Skia does not; this gate is for the browser references.)
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.

Reported, not enforced: WebKit reports the advance box horizontally and Skia whole pixels of a hinted raster, so the references are 1 px apart at the median and 20 px at p99. Judge ink against Chromium.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.
Smart-mode layouts must choose the same lines as the reference in 99.9% of covered cases. Chromium against WebKit is 99.37%.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.
Plain-mode lines came from each browser's own CSS breaker, and the two browsers agree on 97.8% of covered cases. The engine must agree with the reference at least that often.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.
List every case whose fits / does-not-fit decision changed. Not enforced: the decision follows the ink box, where the references themselves differ.
Curved text must set the same glyphs in the same order. Where they sit is reported as numbers.
The solver must choose the same size and lines, with its box within a hundredth of a pixel.

Ink bounds within 2 device px of the reference in 98% of covered pictures. Against WebKit the engine's painter reaches 98.3% (3,612 of 3,675); Chromium against WebKit is 92.8%. What is left is WebKit's own blur filter, its 3 px offset on unrotated supersampled text, and 11 pictures where the reference cuts ink that reaches past the advance and the engine's picture holds it.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.

No disagreement wider than 3 device px in 97% of covered pictures. A region one device pixel wide measures 2 and is antialiasing; above 3 a stroke or a glyph is in a different place. Against WebKit the engine's painter reaches 97.4% (3,578 of 3,675); Chromium against WebKit is 90.4%.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.

Reported, not enforced. The engine paints the font's outline (decision D4); both Mac browsers draw text 11 to 14% heavier (font smoothing), so the overlap with WebKit is under 0.95 for a third of the pictures at size 16 and above (2,104 of 3,162 pass) while the ink box and the thickness gates hold. The two browsers overlap 97% at the median.
Fallback glyphs measure the host; report separately.
